sub.en: Look at the sentences. When do you add -er, when do you use more, and what happens with as … as?

items.q: She’s ___ than her brother.
items.why: Short adjectives take -er / the -est. Long ones take more / the most. good → better / the best.

items.q: He’s ___ than anybody I know.
She’s ___ person in the office.
He’s ___ hard-working ___ she is.
items.why: as … as says the two are equal. With not, it says the first is less.

items.q: She isn’t ___ shy ___ people think.
He’s ___ more confident than he was.
items.why: much / a lot / a bit go in front of a comparative — not very.

items.q: The book was ___ than the film.
There are ___ introverts in this room than you think.
items.why: RECYCLED: more works as a quantifier too — more people, more time.

acts.title: The quiet ones
text: For about thirty years, the ideal employee has been the confident one: sociable, quick to speak, comfortable in a large room. Job advertisements still ask for it. But a best-selling book by the American writer Susan Cain argued that between a third and a half of us are introverts, and that most workplaces are built for the other half.

An introvert is not the same as a shy person. Shyness is a fear of what other people think. Being an introvert is simpler: you get your energy from being alone, and a long day with people leaves you emptier than it leaves an extrovert. Some introverts are much more confident in a meeting than the extroverts around them. They just want to go home afterwards.

Cain’s argument is not that introverts are better. It is that offices are less fair than they look. The person who speaks first is not always the person with the best idea, and the open-plan office — noisier, brighter and more social than any office of the 1970s — is the worst possible room for about half the people in it.
Her practical advice is smaller than the argument: give people the question before the meeting, not during it. The quiet ones will have the answer. They will not shout it across the table.

items.q: What has the ideal employee been for thirty years?
How many of us are introverts, according to the book?
o: between a third and a half

items.q: What is the difference from shyness?
o: shyness is a fear of what others think

items.q: Some introverts in a meeting are
Cain’s argument is that offices are
Her practical advice is to
o: give the question before the meeting

tts: I share a flat with another student called Max. The thing about Max is that he likes everything to be in the correct place.
So he always washes up straight after eating, puts the dishes straight back in the cupboard, never leaves anything on the floor. He even puts his books in alphabetical order in the bookcase.

The other thing about Max is that he never, ever tells a lie. So for example, if he doesn’t like something I’m wearing, he says so. He’s much more honest than most people, and it isn’t always comfortable.

items.s: Max likes everything in the correct place.
He leaves the washing-up until the morning.
His books are in alphabetical order.
He tells small lies to be polite.
The speaker says his honesty is always comfortable.

write.q: Compare two people you know: 6 sentences. Use one short comparative with -er, one long comparative with more, one superlative, one as … as, and one much or a bit before a comparative.
write.model: My sister is quieter than I am, but she isn’t shy. She’s much more confident than me in a room full of strangers — she just leaves earlier. My brother is the most patient person in our family; he can wait for anything. He’s as hard-working as my sister, although he talks about it a lot more. I’m a bit more sociable than both of them and I get tired faster. The strange part is that people always think I’m the quiet one.

speak.q: Compare two people out loud in four sentences: one with a comparative, one with a superlative, one with as … as, and one with much or a bit.
speak.model: My brother is quieter than my sister. My sister is the most sociable person in our family. He’s as hard-working as she is. But she’s a bit more confident with new people.
